faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a modified bitumen roof in Orange?

runs.v: Yes on commercial and multi-family buildings once work exceeds 25% of the roof area in 12 months, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7; a detached one- or two-family reroof is ordinary maintenance. Confirm with the City of Orange Township construction office.

faqs.q: Does modified bitumen roofing in a historic district need extra approval?

runs.v: It can: a property in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the City of Orange Township construction office before work begins.

faqs.q: What is the difference between APP and SBS modified bitumen?

runs.v: SBS modified bitumen provides flexibility, while APP modified bitumen offers strength and UV resistance but is stiffer in cold, per ARMA modified-bitumen guidance.

faqs.q: Do you use torch application on occupied Orange buildings?

runs.v: No. On occupied buildings, Newark Quality Roofing uses self-adhered SBS or cold-adhesive methods, per NRCA hot-work guidance.

faqs.q: Can modified bitumen be installed over an existing flat roof in Orange?

runs.v: It can recover a sound roof without full tear-off, but the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode requires complete removal when the roof is water-soaked or deteriorated, is wood shake, slate, clay, cement, or asbestos-cement tile, or already carries two or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.
